Right now, yes. `transfer` changes the owner but leaves the old approval in place, so Fen can take the Duskling from its new keeper. An approval should end when the Duskling changes hands.

**Task:**

1. In `transfer`, after changing the owner, reset `approved` to `None`.

### Trade day

URL: https://dusklings.com/hatchery.html#trade-day

Your finished contract is running. Approve Fen, let Fen collect, and try the loophole you just closed.

### The code at the end of lesson 5

```rust
#![no_std]

extern crate alloc;

use bytecheck::CheckBytes;
use dusk_core::signatures::bls::PublicKey as BlsPublicKey;
use dusk_forge::ContractEvent;
use rkyv::{Archive, Deserialize, Serialize};

/// A Duskling hatched.
#[derive(Archive, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[archive_attr(derive(CheckBytes))]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "data-driver", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
pub struct Hatched {
    pub id: u64,
    pub dna: u64,
}

impl ContractEvent for Hatched {
    const TOPICS: &'static [&'static str] = &["hatched"];
}

/// A Duskling came back from a hunt.
#[derive(Archive, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[archive_attr(derive(CheckBytes))]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "data-driver", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
pub struct Hunted {
    pub id: u64,
    pub moth_id: u64,
}

impl ContractEvent for Hunted {
    const TOPICS: &'static [&'static str] = &["hunted"];
}

/// A Duskling changed hands.
#[derive(Archive, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[archive_attr(derive(CheckBytes))]
#[cfg_attr(feature = "data-driver", derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize))]
pub struct Transferred {
    pub id: u64,
    pub to: BlsPublicKey,
}

impl ContractEvent for Transferred {
    const TOPICS: &'static [&'static str] = &["transferred"];
}

#[dusk_forge::contract(events = [crate::Hatched, crate::Hunted, crate::Transferred])]
mod hatchery {
    use alloc::vec::Vec;
    use dusk_core::abi::{self, ContractId};
    use dusk_core::signatures::bls::PublicKey as BlsPublicKey;

    const DNA_DIGITS: u32 = 16;
    const DNA_MODULUS: u64 = 10u64.pow(DNA_DIGITS);
    // 2^64 divided by the golden ratio: a classic mixing constant.
    const MIX: u64 = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15;
    // The Moth Nest: another team's contract on the same chain.
    const MOTH_NEST: ContractId = ContractId::from_bytes([7; 32]);
    const COOLDOWN: u64 = 360;

    struct Duskling {
        dna: u64,
        level: u32,
        owner: BlsPublicKey,
        ready_at: u64,
        wins: u32,
        losses: u32,
        approved: Option<BlsPublicKey>,
    }

    pub struct Hatchery {
        dusklings: Vec<Duskling>,
    }

    impl Hatchery {
        pub const fn new() -> Self {
            Self { dusklings: Vec::new() }
        }

        fn create_duskling(&mut self, dna: u64, owner: BlsPublicKey) {
            let id = self.dusklings.len() as u64;
            self.dusklings.push(Duskling { dna, level: 1, owner, ready_at: 0, wins: 0, losses: 0, approved: None });
            abi::emit("hatched", crate::Hatched { id, dna });
        }

        fn generate_dna(&self, seed: u64) -> u64 {
            seed.wrapping_mul(MIX) % DNA_MODULUS
        }

        pub fn hatch(&mut self, seed: u64) {
            let keeper = abi::public_sender().expect("Hatch from a public Moonlight account");
            assert!(self.dusklings_of(keeper) == 0, "Every keeper hatches one Duskling");
            let dna = self.generate_dna(seed);
            self.create_duskling(dna, keeper);
        }

        pub fn duskling_count(&self) -> u64 {
            self.dusklings.len() as u64
        }

        pub fn dna_of(&self, id: u64) -> Option<u64> {
            self.dusklings.get(id as usize).map(|d| d.dna)
        }

        pub fn owner_of(&self, id: u64) -> Option<BlsPublicKey> {
            self.dusklings.get(id as usize).map(|d| d.owner)
        }

        pub fn dusklings_of(&self, keeper: BlsPublicKey) -> u64 {
            self.dusklings.iter().filter(|d| d.owner == keeper).count() as u64
        }

        fn moth_dna(&self, moth_id: u64) -> u64 {
            abi::call::<_, u64>(MOTH_NEST, "moth_dna", &moth_id).expect("The Moth Nest has no such moth")
        }

        fn blend(&self, dna: u64, moth: u64) -> u64 {
            let mixed = (dna + moth) / 2;
            mixed - mixed % 100 + 99
        }

        pub fn hunt(&mut self, id: u64, moth_id: u64) {
            let keeper = self.only_keeper(id);
            assert!(self.is_ready(id), "Your Duskling is still resting");
            let hunter = &self.dusklings[id as usize];
            let dna = self.blend(hunter.dna, self.moth_dna(moth_id));
            self.create_duskling(dna, keeper);
            abi::emit("hunted", crate::Hunted { id, moth_id });
            self.dusklings[id as usize].ready_at = abi::block_height() + COOLDOWN;
        }

        fn is_ready(&self, id: u64) -> bool {
            abi::block_height() >= self.dusklings[id as usize].ready_at
        }

        fn only_keeper(&self, id: u64) -> BlsPublicKey {
            let keeper = abi::public_sender().expect("Use a public Moonlight account");
            let duskling = self.dusklings.get(id as usize).expect("No such Duskling");
            assert!(duskling.owner == keeper, "Only its keeper can do that");
            keeper
        }

        fn roll(&self, id: u64, target: u64) -> u64 {
            id.wrapping_mul(MIX)
                .wrapping_add(target)
                .wrapping_add(abi::block_height())
                .wrapping_mul(MIX)
                % 100
        }

        pub fn battle(&mut self, id: u64, target: u64) {
            self.only_keeper(id);
            assert!(self.is_ready(id), "Your Duskling is still resting");
            assert!(id != target && (target as usize) < self.dusklings.len(), "Pick another Duskling to battle");
            let roll = self.roll(id, target);
            if roll < 70 {
                self.dusklings[id as usize].wins += 1;
                self.dusklings[id as usize].level += 1;
                self.dusklings[target as usize].losses += 1;
            } else {
                self.dusklings[id as usize].losses += 1;
                self.dusklings[target as usize].wins += 1;
            }
            self.dusklings[id as usize].ready_at = abi::block_height() + COOLDOWN;
        }

        pub fn transfer(&mut self, id: u64, to: BlsPublicKey) {
            self.only_keeper(id);
            self.dusklings[id as usize].owner = to;
            self.dusklings[id as usize].approved = None;
            abi::emit("transferred", crate::Transferred { id, to });
        }

        pub fn approve(&mut self, id: u64, to: BlsPublicKey) {
            self.only_keeper(id);
            self.dusklings[id as usize].approved = Some(to);
        }

        pub fn take(&mut self, id: u64) {
            let taker = abi::public_sender().expect("Use a public Moonlight account");
            let duskling = &mut self.dusklings[id as usize];
            assert!(duskling.approved == Some(taker), "You're not approved to take this Duskling");
            duskling.owner = taker;
            duskling.approved = None;
        }
    }
}
```

# The Almanac

Build a JavaScript dApp that reads a Dusk contract with Dusk Connect and its data-driver, then prepares hatch and transfer calls for a wallet to sign.

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html

## Lesson 1: The Almanac

### A book of every Duskling

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#almanac-intro

A **dApp** is an app whose data lives in a contract. You'll write its data layer in JavaScript with **Dusk Connect**, Dusk's browser SDK, and the Hatchery's **data-driver**. The data-driver is a small WebAssembly module Forge builds from the contract, and it knows how to encode arguments and decode results.

Reading a contract is a **query** that a node runs for you: no wallet, no transaction and no fee.

### Your first read

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#count

`createApp` is already written. It points Dusk Connect at a node and at the Hatchery, and gives the contract the short name `"hatchery"`.

To call a read-only function, name the contract and the function:

```js
await dusk.readContract({ contract: "hatchery", functionName: "…" })
```

**Task:**

1. In `countDusklings`, return the result of reading `duskling_count`.

### Why a string?

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#exact-count

A Rust `u64` goes up to about 18 quintillion. A JavaScript number holds whole numbers exactly only up to 2^53, about 9 quadrillion. Beyond that it rounds.

So the Hatchery's data-driver sends a returned `u64` as a **string** of digits, keeping every one. `BigInt` turns it into an exact whole number you can compare and do math with.

**Task:**

1. Store the result in `const count`, then return `BigInt(count)`.

### Asking about one Duskling

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#dna

Functions with parameters take `args`. `dna_of(id)` returns an `Option<u64>`: the DNA, or `null` when there's no Duskling with that ID.

The Hatchery's driver reads `u64` arguments as JSON numbers. A small ID like 3 can simply be a number.

```js
await dusk.readContract({ contract: "hatchery", functionName: "…", args: id })
```

**Task:**

1. In `readDna`, return the result of `dna_of` with `args: id`.

### Whose is it?

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#owner

`owner_of(id)` returns the keeper's public key, or `null`. The driver writes a key as a long base58 string.

> A public key identifies an account, not a person. It's also public: anyone can run this same query.

**Task:**

1. In `readOwner`, return the result of `owner_of` for `id`.

### Filling the Almanac

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#gallery

Now put the reads together. Loop over every ID below the count and collect each Duskling.

`id < count` compares a number with a BigInt, which JavaScript allows. IDs stay small, so plain numbers are fine as arguments.

**Task:**

1. In `listDusklings`, get the count, then for each `id` from 0 up to the count, push `{ id, dna, owner }` using your read functions. Return the list.

### Every digit counts

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#digits

Duskling #3's real DNA is `9437186547890123`, but the Almanac shows `9437186547890124`. That's larger than 2^53, and `dna_of` returns an `Option<u64>`. The driver only sends a *top-level* `u64` as a string. Anything nested, like this `Option`, arrives as a plain JSON number. Dusk Connect parses it into a JavaScript number, and those round anything above 2^53.

The app can't get the digits back. It can refuse to trust them: `Number.isSafeInteger(n)` is `true` only for whole numbers small enough to be sure they're exact.

> The real fix is on the contract side: return a plain `u64` for values apps must read exactly, and the driver sends every digit as a string.

**Task:**

1. In the loop, store the DNA in `const dna` and add `exact: Number.isSafeInteger(dna)` to each entry.

### When the node is down

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#offline

Nodes can be unreachable. A failed read throws, and that's different from a missing Duskling, which is a successful answer of `null`.

Catch the failure where the page loads, so the Almanac can say “try again” instead of crashing:

```js
try { … } catch (error) { … }
```

**Task:**

1. In `loadAlmanac`, wrap the existing return in `try`, and in `catch` return `{ status: "unavailable" }`.

### The finished Almanac

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#almanac-lab

Your data layer is feeding a real page. Every card here comes from your own `loadAlmanac`, running Dusk Connect and the Hatchery's data-driver against the practice node.

### The code at the end of lesson 1

```js
const { createDuskApp } = await import(
  new URL("/academy/vendor/dusk-connect.js", location.origin).href
);

// Connects to a node and to the Hatchery contract through its data-driver.
export function createApp(nodeUrl, contractId) {
  return createDuskApp({
    pinnedNodeUrl: nodeUrl,
    autoConnect: false,
    wallet: { waitForProvider: false, rememberLastUsedProvider: false },
    contracts: {
      hatchery: {
        contractId,
        driverUrl: new URL("/drivers/hatchery.wasm", nodeUrl).href,
      },
    },
  });
}

export async function countDusklings(dusk) {
  const count = await dusk.readContract({ contract: "hatchery", functionName: "duskling_count" });
  return BigInt(count);
}

export async function readDna(dusk, id) {
  return await dusk.readContract({ contract: "hatchery", functionName: "dna_of", args: id });
}

export async function readOwner(dusk, id) {
  return await dusk.readContract({ contract: "hatchery", functionName: "owner_of", args: id });
}

export async function listDusklings(dusk) {
  const count = await countDusklings(dusk);
  const dusklings = [];
  for (let id = 0; id < count; id++) {
    const dna = await readDna(dusk, id);
    dusklings.push({ id, dna, owner: await readOwner(dusk, id), exact: Number.isSafeInteger(dna) });
  }
  return dusklings;
}

export async function loadAlmanac(dusk) {
  try {
    return { status: "ok", dusklings: await listDusklings(dusk) };
  } catch (error) {
    return { status: "unavailable" };
  }
}
```

## Lesson 2: Hatching from the web

### From reading to writing

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#web-intro

A dApp never signs anything itself. It **prepares** a contract call: which contract, which function, the encoded arguments and the options. Then it hands that to the keeper's **wallet**, which asks the keeper to approve, signs and sends it.

This course has no wallet and sends nothing. You'll prepare calls and look at exactly what a wallet would be asked to sign.

### Preparing a hatch

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#prepare-hatch

`prepareContractCall` encodes the arguments with the data-driver and returns the call's parameters:

```js
await dusk.prepareContractCall({
  contract: "hatchery", functionName: "…", args: …,
  privacy: "public", amount: "0", deposit: "0",
});
```

- `privacy` is required. The Hatchery's `hatch` calls `abi::public_sender()`, so a shielded call would panic. It must be `"public"`.
- `amount` and `deposit` are DUSK values, counted in Lux, DUSK's smallest unit. `deposit` is what the called contract can collect. `hatch` doesn't take any DUSK, so both are `"0"`. The keeper still pays gas: fees are separate from these values.

**Task:**

1. In `prepareHatch`, return a prepared call to `hatch` with `args: seed`, public privacy, and no DUSK attached.

### A seed from a name

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#seed-name

This site turns your Duskling's name into its seed with **FNV-1a**, a small, well-known hash. You can do the same in the app, so the page knows the seed before anyone hatches.

For each byte: XOR it into the hash (`^=`), multiply by the FNV prime, and keep 64 bits by masking (`& 0xffffffffffffffffn`). The `n` suffix makes a BigInt, so nothing rounds.

**Task:**

1. Inside the loop in `seedFromName`, add `hash ^= BigInt(byte);`
2. Then `hash = (hash * 0x100000001b3n) & 0xffffffffffffffffn;`

### Arguments that keep every digit

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#exact-seed

Try hatching with that seed: Dusk Connect turns a BigInt into a JSON *string*, and the driver wants a JSON *number*, so it refuses. A plain number would round a seed this big.

`JSON.rawJSON("…")` gives Dusk Connect raw JSON number text, so every digit reaches the driver.

```js
args: JSON.rawJSON(seed.toString())
```

**Task:**

1. In `prepareHatch`, change `args: seed` to `args: JSON.rawJSON(seed.toString())`.

### Several arguments

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#prepare-transfer

`transfer(id, to)` takes two parameters. Forge bundles several parameters into a tuple, so pass them as an array, in order: `args: [id, to]`.

`to` is a keeper's key: the same base58 string `readOwner` returns.

**Task:**

1. In `prepareTransfer`, return a prepared call to `transfer` with `args: [id, to]`, public, with no DUSK attached.

### Your hatch request

URL: https://dusklings.com/almanac.html#hatch-lab

This is your own `seedFromName` and `prepareHatch` at work. A wallet would show this request, ask you to approve it, then sign and send it. This page stops here: nothing is sent.

> In this practice Hatchery you already keep two Dusklings. A keeper who has one can't hatch another, so the contract would refuse this call.

### The code at the end of lesson 2

```js
const { createDuskApp } = await import(
  new URL("/academy/vendor/dusk-connect.js", location.origin).href
);

// Connects to a node and to the Hatchery contract through its data-driver.
export function createApp(nodeUrl, contractId) {
  return createDuskApp({
    pinnedNodeUrl: nodeUrl,
    autoConnect: false,
    wallet: { waitForProvider: false, rememberLastUsedProvider: false },
    contracts: {
      hatchery: {
        contractId,
        driverUrl: new URL("/drivers/hatchery.wasm", nodeUrl).href,
      },
    },
  });
}

export async function countDusklings(dusk) {
  const count = await dusk.readContract({ contract: "hatchery", functionName: "duskling_count" });
  return BigInt(count);
}

export async function readDna(dusk, id) {
  return await dusk.readContract({ contract: "hatchery", functionName: "dna_of", args: id });
}

export async function readOwner(dusk, id) {
  return await dusk.readContract({ contract: "hatchery", functionName: "owner_of", args: id });
}

export async function listDusklings(dusk) {
  const count = await countDusklings(dusk);
  const dusklings = [];
  for (let id = 0; id < count; id++) {
    const dna = await readDna(dusk, id);
    dusklings.push({ id, dna, owner: await readOwner(dusk, id), exact: Number.isSafeInteger(dna) });
  }
  return dusklings;
}

export async function loadAlmanac(dusk) {
  try {
    return { status: "ok", dusklings: await listDusklings(dusk) };
  } catch (error) {
    return { status: "unavailable" };
  }
}

export async function prepareHatch(dusk, seed) {
  return await dusk.prepareContractCall({
    contract: "hatchery",
    functionName: "hatch",
    args: JSON.rawJSON(seed.toString()),
    privacy: "public",
    amount: "0",
    deposit: "0",
  });
}

export function seedFromName(name) {
  let hash = 0xcbf29ce484222325n;
  for (const byte of new TextEncoder().encode(name)) {
    hash ^= BigInt(byte);
    hash = (hash * 0x100000001b3n) & 0xffffffffffffffffn;
  }
  return hash;
}

export async function prepareTransfer(dusk, id, to) {
  return await dusk.prepareContractCall({
    contract: "hatchery",
    functionName: "transfer",
    args: [id, to],
    privacy: "public",
    amount: "0",
    deposit: "0",
  });
}
```

# Secret stats

Write dusk-plonk circuits that prove a Duskling's power without revealing its stats, then that it's at least 50. Each check makes a real PLONK proof.

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html

## Lesson 1: Secret stats

### Show nothing, prove everything

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#stats-intro

In this path you'll write a **circuit**: a set of mathematical rules that a zero-knowledge proof shows were followed.

The **prover** knows the secret values. The **verifier** checks the proof against the circuit and a few **public inputs**, and learns nothing else.

You'll use **dusk-plonk**, Dusk's PLONK library. Your browser will generate and check real proofs.

### Private inputs

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#witnesses

A circuit's secret inputs are called **witnesses**. `composer.append_witness(value)` adds one and returns a **handle** that later gates can refer to.

Circuit values are `BlsScalar`s: numbers in the finite field that dusk-plonk works in.

```rust
let luck = composer.append_witness(self.luck);
```

**Task:**

1. Replace the comment with two witnesses: `strength` from `self.strength`, then `agility` from `self.agility`.

### An addition gate

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#add-gate

A **gate** is a rule relating witnesses. `gate_add` takes a `Constraint` describing a weighted sum, and returns a handle to the result:

```rust
let total = composer.gate_add(
    Constraint::new().left(1).right(1).a(x).b(y)
);
```

`left` and `right` are the weights for `a` and `b`, so this computes 1·x + 1·y.

**Task:**

1. Add `let sum = …`: an addition gate over `strength` and `agility`, both with weight 1.

### The claimed power

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#claim

Next, the value the arena cares about: power. Allocate it as another witness.

When you check this chapter, your browser really proves the circuit for three keepers. Watch closely what happens to Rook's claim.

**Task:**

1. After the gate, add `let power = composer.append_witness(self.power);`

### Tie it together

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#bind

Allocating `power` didn't connect it to anything, so it can be any number. `assert_equal` adds an **equality constraint**: the proof is only valid if both handles hold the same value.

```rust
composer.assert_equal(a, b);
```

> A Rust `assert!` wouldn't do this. It only runs on the prover's machine while the circuit is built, so a cheating prover could just delete it. A constraint is part of what the verifier checks.

**Task:**

1. Constrain `sum` and `power` to be equal.

### Show the verifier the power

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#public

The arena needs to know which power a proof is about. So far power is a secret witness too, and the proof doesn't say which power it covers.

`append_public` makes a value a **public input**: the verifier supplies it when checking, and the proof only verifies for that exact value. Keep strength and agility as witnesses.

> Rust's `pub` on a struct field controls which code can access it. It has nothing to do with what a proof reveals.

**Task:**

1. Change power's allocation to `composer.append_public(self.power)`. Keep the equality constraint.

### Prove your Duskling's power

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#stats-proof

Your circuit from this lesson is ready. Generate a real PLONK proof for your own Duskling, then try to cheat with it.

> This proof says the prover knows *some* strength and agility that add up to power. Nothing ties them to a particular Duskling yet: Rook could simply claim 30 + 20. A real game would keep stats off-chain and commit to them, for example with a hash stored in the Hatchery, then prove the stats match it. Here, your stats are worked out from your Duskling's DNA just so you have numbers to play with, and DNA is public.

### The code at the end of lesson 1

```rust
use dusk_plonk::prelude::*;

// Your Duskling's stats. strength and agility stay secret.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct SecretStats {
    pub strength: BlsScalar,
    pub agility: BlsScalar,
    pub power: BlsScalar,
}

impl Circuit for SecretStats {
    fn circuit(&self, composer: &mut Composer) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let strength = composer.append_witness(self.strength);
        let agility = composer.append_witness(self.agility);
        let sum = composer.gate_add(Constraint::new().left(1).right(1).a(strength).b(agility));
        let power = composer.append_public(self.power);
        composer.assert_equal(sum, power);
        Ok(())
    }
}
```

## Lesson 2: The arena pass

### Fifty or more

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#pass-intro

Proving a **threshold** without revealing the number is a classic zero-knowledge job. It's the same idea as proving you're old enough without showing your birthday.

You'll hide power again, add a helper witness, and learn why numbers in a circuit can wrap around, and how a **range check** stops that.

### Power goes private

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#hide-power

For the arena pass, the proof shouldn't reveal power at all. It should only show that the rules hold. Turn power back into a witness.

The circuit itself is public, so the arena knows exactly which rules a valid proof satisfied.

**Task:**

1. Change power back to `composer.append_witness(self.power)`.

### A helper witness

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#slack

To show power ≥ 50, the prover supplies the difference as another witness: `slack = power − 50`.

`BlsScalar` supports subtraction, and `BlsScalar::from(50u64)` turns a number into a field value.

```rust
let bonus = composer.append_witness(self.luck - BlsScalar::from(7u64));
```

**Task:**

1. At the end of the circuit, allocate `slack` as a witness holding `self.power - BlsScalar::from(50u64)`.

### Check the helper

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#floor

A cheating prover can put any value in `slack`, so the circuit must check it. Rebuild power from it: `slack + 50`, using a **constant** term, and require it to equal power.

```rust
let plus_seven = composer.gate_add(Constraint::new().left(1).constant(7).a(bonus));
```

**Task:**

1. Add `let floor = …`: a gate computing `slack + 50` (weight 1 on `slack`, constant 50).
2. Constrain `floor` and `power` to be equal.

### Keep slack small

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#range

Numbers in a circuit live in a **finite field**, where there's no going below zero: `23 − 50` wraps around to a 77-digit number. So “slack exists” proves nothing until you also prove it's small.

`component_range::<8>(w)` constrains `w` to 8 bit pairs, that is 16 bits: 0 to 65,535. A wrapped-around slack is far bigger, so no valid proof can be made.

**Task:**

1. Add `composer.component_range::<8>(slack);` at the end of the circuit.

### Your arena pass

URL: https://dusklings.com/secret-stats.html#pass-proof

Generate an arena pass for your own Duskling with the circuit you just finished.

> This pass isn't tied to you or to tonight, so anyone who copied it could reuse it. A real pass would add a public input, such as a session number or a commitment to the keeper, so each proof only works where it's meant to. That's the same idea as “Valid isn't forever” in the keeper's journey.

### The code at the end of lesson 2

```rust
use dusk_plonk::prelude::*;

// Your Duskling's stats. strength and agility stay secret.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct SecretStats {
    pub strength: BlsScalar,
    pub agility: BlsScalar,
    pub power: BlsScalar,
}

impl Circuit for SecretStats {
    fn circuit(&self, composer: &mut Composer) -> Result<(), Error> {
        let strength = composer.append_witness(self.strength);
        let agility = composer.append_witness(self.agility);
        let sum = composer.gate_add(Constraint::new().left(1).right(1).a(strength).b(agility));
        let power = composer.append_witness(self.power);
        composer.assert_equal(sum, power);
        let slack = composer.append_witness(self.power - BlsScalar::from(50u64));
        let floor = composer.gate_add(Constraint::new().left(1).constant(50).a(slack));
        composer.assert_equal(floor, power);
        composer.component_range::<8>(slack);
        Ok(())
    }
}
```
